Class ExprToTHF

java.lang.Object
com.articulate.sigma.parsing.ExprToTHF
public class ExprToTHF extends Object
Translates Expr trees to THF (Typed Higher-order Form) TPTP syntax.

THF differs from FOF/TFF in two key ways:

  1. Function/relation application uses curried @ syntax: (s__pred @ arg1 @ arg2) instead of s__pred(arg1,arg2).
  2. Quantifiers carry full type annotations: ! [V__X:$i, V__W:w] : body instead of ! [V__X] : body.

Type information for variables is supplied as a Map<String, Set<String>> where the key is the KIF variable name (e.g. "?X") and the value is a set of SUMO type strings (e.g. {"World"}, {"Formula"}). The set is interpreted by thfType(String, Map, boolean) to produce one of the four THF base types: $i (individual), $o (boolean), w (Kripke world) or m (modal accessibility relation).

This class is the Expr-based counterpart of THFnew.process(com.articulate.sigma.Formula, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>>, boolean) (modal) and THFnew.processNonModal(com.articulate.sigma.Formula, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>>, boolean) (plain).

    • translate

      public static String translate(Expr expr, boolean query, Map<String,Set<String>> typeMap)
      Translate an Expr tree to a THF formula string (modal embedding).

      Free variables are wrapped in a typed universal (or existential) quantifier.

      Parameters:
      expr - the formula tree; may already contain world-argument nodes injected by Modals.processModalsExpr(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, com.articulate.sigma.KB)
      query - true → free vars get ? (existential), else !
      typeMap - variable → set-of-SUMO-types, built by FormulaPreprocessor.findTypeRestrictionsExpr(com.articulate.sigma.parsing.Expr, com.articulate.sigma.KB) plus world-variable entries from modal processing
      Returns:
      the THF formula string

    • translateNonModal

      public static String translateNonModal(Expr expr, boolean query, Map<String,Set<String>> typeMap)
      Translate an Expr tree to a THF formula string (non-modal / plain mode).

      No world or modal types are used; variables are either $i or $o.

      Parameters:
      expr - the formula tree
      query - true → free vars get existential quantifier
      typeMap - variable type hints (only "Formula" is honoured to assign $o; everything else maps to $i)
      Returns:
      the THF formula string

    • translateAccrelnTHF

      private static String translateAccrelnTHF(Expr.SExpr se, Map<String,Set<String>> typeMap, boolean modalMode)
      Translate an accreln2 or accreln3 application.

      These accessibility-relation predicates are produced by the Kripke modal rewrite:

      • accreln2(pred, agent, W1, W2) — for binary HOL predicates
      • accreln3(pred, a1, a2, W1, W2) — for ternary HOL predicates
      The first argument is always the modal operator itself (e.g. holdsDuring, believes) which has type m in the header. It must be translated in head position (no __m suffix) to preserve that type; using argument-position translation would produce s__holdsDuring__m : $i which mismatches the m type expected by accreln2/3.

      This mirrors the old processRecurse() guard in THFnew.java that set hasArguments = true for regHOLpred / regHOL3pred atoms.

    • thfType

      public static String thfType(String kifVar, Map<String,Set<String>> typeMap, boolean modalMode)
      Map a KIF variable name to its THF base type.

      In modal mode:

      • ?W<digits> → w (Kripke world variable, by naming convention)
      • type-set contains "Formula" → (w > $o)
      • type-set contains "World" → w
      • type-set contains "Modal" → m
      • otherwise → $i

      In non-modal mode:

      • type-set contains "Formula" → $o
      • otherwise → $i

      This replicates the logic of THFnew.getTHFtype(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>>) and THFnew.getTHFtypeNonModal(java.lang.String, java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.util.Set<java.lang.String>>) without introducing a dependency from the parsing package to the trans package.
